subject: EdgeScale capacity ops playbook and deployment pathing
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: EdgeScale capacity ops playbook and initial asks

Thanks for the time earlier this morning — appreciated the clear signals on latency objectives and the expected traffic shape. Recap + asks below so we have a single place to iterate. I attached the first-pass capacity workbook and a short SOC2 summary for your security team; draft MAP attached as well.

Call recap (30-minute discovery):
- Primary use case: API layer for personalized recommendations + short-form generation (customer-facing).
- Target SLO: p95 latency <= 120ms for <2k token responses; p95 <= 300ms for long tails.
- Traffic profile you mentioned: baseline 35 TPS, predictable daily peak ~110 TPS, 5-10 minute bursts up to ~200 TPS around promos.
- Token mix: heavy short queries (~70% <=64 tokens), mid-length ~20% (65-512), long ~10% (>=512 up to 2k). Avg tokens per request ~420.

Deployment pathing options we discussed: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated reserved pool (predictable, isolated), Private VPC (if you need network isolation + on-prem later). You flagged procurement + SOC questions as gating for Dedicated.

Immediate asks from EdgeScale (action items for us to confirm):
1) Recommended GPU type and rough count for Dedicated to hit 110 TPS sustained with safety for bursts to 200 TPS (please confirm if 110 is sustained or just peak-of-day).
2) Expected concurrency per GPU and batching parameters that meet your latency SLOs.
3) Any hard security controls needed beyond SOC2 (we attached a summary; Lauren, can you help pick the right doc for their security team?).
4) Timeline for pilot (two-week reserved pilot vs a hosted ramp).

Next steps I propose:
- We (Markus + Monica) will provide a conservative Dedicated sizing estimate and a small configuration playbook (GPU type, instance mix, expected TPS per-GPU, quantization/kv-cache guidance) by EOD today. (See attached workbook v1).
- Aditya will follow up with draft commercial terms for a reserved pilot and a short MAP with milestones.
- Samira/Ben: please confirm whether 110 TPS is your sustained day peak or a short burst number and whether the SOC2 summary is sufficient for initial procurement review.

Attachments: EdgeScale_Capacity_Workbook_v1.xlsx; SOC2-Redwood-Summary.pdf; draft_MAP_edgescale.docx

Thanks — more detail coming shortly from Monica on GPU choices.

— Markus
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Thanks Markus — quick clarifications:
- 110 TPS is our expected sustained peak during business hours (roughly 9a–6p US ET with regional concentration), not a one-off spike. Bursts to 200 TPS are expected for 3–6 minute windows during new feature launches.
- Latency targets are firm for customer-facing endpoints: p95 <= 120ms for typical short responses, acceptable p95 up to 300ms for long tails.
- Security: SOC2 summary is helpful; our security team may ask about key management (KMS/HSM) and audit log retention windows (we'll push specifics if needed).

One other ask: we'd like an estimate of expected monthly cost range for Dedicated vs Hosted for the config you propose (rough ballpark is fine).

Subject: Technical note: Dedicated sizing assumptions and recommended config

Samira / Markus — following our call, I updated the capacity workbook (attached as part of Markus' original email and updated tab "Monica-v1") and captured the technical assumptions we used. Key points below — this is a conservative configuration to meet p95 latency targets while keeping headroom for bursts and maintenance.

High-level recommendation (Dedicated reserved pool):
- GPU selection: H100 80GB (preferred) for best throughput on long-context workloads; A100 80GB as acceptable alternative if H100 availability is constrained.
- Model variant: fp16 / int8-quantized where applicable; keep an unquantized fallback for high-quality long-generation requests.
- Suggested pool sizing for sustained 110 TPS baseline, bursts up to 200 TPS:
  - H100-80GB nodes: start with 6 GPUs (3 nodes x 2 GPUs) with per-GPU concurrency ~10 ongoing streams (depending on avg token length) and batching window tuned to 8–15ms to preserve p95.
  - Expected effective TPS per H100 (avg token mix described): ~18–22 TPS (conservative); with 6 GPUs -> 108–132 TPS sustained. Bursts handled with autoscaling + short-lived burst capacity (additional 2 GPUs on warm standby).
  - If using A100-80GB, plan for ~15–18 TPS per GPU -> 8 GPUs recommended.

Concurrency and batching notes:
- Concurrency targets are driven by token mix. With ~70% short queries, we can push higher per-GPU concurrency without hitting p95. For mixed workloads, we recommend per-GPU concurrency caps and request routing: short-query pool vs long-context pool.
- KV cache: enable prefix caching for repeated contexts (recommend keeping KV cache memory fraction high for low-latency recs).
- Quantization: int8 gives 1.6–2x throughput improvement on H100/A100 for the model family you're evaluating; reserve 10–20% of traffic on higher-fidelity FP16 to monitor quality drift during pilot.

Latency expectations (approx):
- Short (<=64 tokens): p95 ~40–90ms depending on batch visibility windows.
- Mid (65–512 tokens): p95 ~100–220ms.
- Long (>512 tokens): p95 ~200–350ms (use long-context pool to reduce variance).

Pilot recommendation:
- Two-week reserved pilot with the 6x H100 configuration (or 8x A100 if needed) and a 2-GPU warm standby for bursts; include a canary routing policy to test quality-sensitive traffic on FP16 vs int8. Monitor token-level costs and p95 per-route.

Attachments referenced: I updated the workbook tab and added a short config snippet (see workbook). I also attached a one-page config playbook to the MAP.

Technical follow-ups I need from EdgeScale:
- Confirm the sustained 110 TPS number (Samira confirmed in reply).
- Provide a sample 24-hour traffic histogram (or point to a telemetry dashboard) if you want more aggressive consolidation.

— Monica
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Commercial / procurement: reserved pilot and cost buckets

Ben / Samira — brief commercial note to align timelines and what we'll need from procurement to spin up the pilot quickly.

1) Pricing buckets (very rough estimate for sizing above) — monthly run-rate (incl. infra + service + support):
   - Dedicated (H100 pool, 6 active GPUs + 2 warm standby): estimate $64k–$95k / month depending on commit level and quantization profile.
   - Hosted (fully-managed dynamic): estimate $95k–$130k / month for equivalent latency SLOs, higher headroom pricing but no reserved commit.
   - Private VPC (customer-managed networking + private control plane): add one-time onboarding + higher base fee; ongoing near Dedicated pricing but adds infra/networking costs.

2) Pilot terms we recommend:
   - Two-week technical pilot with pro-rated billing for reserved capacity + one week of ramp monitoring.
   - MAP milestones: 1) Pilot start, 2) Quality sign-off on sample prompts, 3) Latency SLO verification, 4) Procurement PO for 3-month reserved commitment (if good). Draft MAP attached.

3) Procurement asks from EdgeScale to accelerate:
   - PO template / contact for invoicing.
   - Any additional security docs (if SOC2 summary is insufficient).
   - Expected PO timeline (Ben, does 3/17 look realistic?).

We'll prepare a formal quote and the MAP doc for signature once we have confirmation on the final node count (H100 vs A100) and the pilot start date.

— Aditya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
